pool.text: El Carmen monastery was founded in a small town during the early Spanish colonial period.
The Universidad de San Carlos was established, making it older than most North American universities.
The capital was moved to the current location of Guatemala City in a valley.
Guatemala City hosted the signing of the Act of Independence of Central America from Spain.
Guatemala declared itself an independent republic and Guatemala City became its national capital.
The immense neo-classical Metropolitan Cathedral was completed in the central plaza.
Guatemala City and the surrounding region suffered destruction from earthquakes and months of aftershocks.
The National Palace was built as an official residence and headquarters for the president.
President Ubico was overthrown in the democratic Guatemalan Revolution movement.
Engineer Martin Prado Vélez took over as mayor and ruled the city during reformist presidencies.
A large tremor measuring 7.5 on the moment magnitude scale hit the region.
Heavy rainfalls caused canyon-edge slums to be washed away and buried under mudslides.
A very large, deep circular hole with vertical walls opened in northeastern Guatemala City.
The Pacaya volcano erupted and Tropical Storm Agatha brought torrential downpours simultaneously.
